questions.stem: The primary function of the legislature is to

options.text: appoint judges to the higher courts

questions.explanation: Law making is the defining function from which the legislature takes its name. Its other roles — finance, oversight, representation — support or flow from that central task.

distractorRationale.b: Enforcement belongs to the executive and its agencies
distractorRationale.d: Judges are appointed by the executive on National Judicial Council recommendation, with legislative confirmation only for the highest courts

questions.stem: How many members make up the Senate of the Federal Republic of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Three senators come from each of the 36 states, giving 108, and one more represents the Federal Capital Territory, making 109. The equal allocation per state is what makes the Senate the chamber that represents the federating units.

distractorRationale.a: 36 is the number of states, not of senators
distractorRationale.b: 108 omits the single senator for the Federal Capital Territory
distractorRationale.d: 360 is the size of the House of Representatives

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), section 48

questions.stem: At which stage of a bill's passage is it examined clause by clause, with a public hearing and proposed amendments?
questions.explanation: The committee stage is where detailed work happens: a standing committee takes memoranda, holds a public hearing and reshapes individual clauses. The plenary stages deal with the bill as a whole rather than its details.

distractorRationale.a: At first reading only the title is read and the bill is formally introduced, without debate
distractorRationale.b: The second reading debates the general principles of the bill, not its individual clauses
distractorRationale.d: By the third reading the bill is in final form and is simply passed or rejected

questions.stem: Federations usually adopt a bicameral legislature mainly because a second chamber

options.text: reduces the cost of running the legislature
gives the component units equal representation at the centre
allows bills to be passed more quickly
removes the need for judicial review of legislation

questions.explanation: A chamber based on population would let the most populous units dominate. An upper chamber with equal seats per unit reassures smaller states that they cannot be legislated over, which is essential to holding a federation together.

distractorRationale.a: Two chambers cost more, not less; expense is the standard criticism of bicameralism
distractorRationale.c: Two chambers slow legislation down, which is part of the intended check
distractorRationale.d: Judicial review remains necessary whatever the structure of the legislature

questions.stem: The legislative instrument by which the National Assembly authorises government spending for a financial year is the
questions.explanation: The Appropriation Act is the budget in legal form: it authorises withdrawals from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for stated purposes. Without it the executive has no lawful authority to spend, which is the legislature's strongest single check.

distractorRationale.b: A Finance Act changes tax and revenue law rather than authorising expenditure
distractorRationale.c: The Electoral Act regulates the conduct of elections
distractorRationale.d: The Public Procurement Act governs how contracts are awarded once funds are appropriated

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), sections 80 to 82

questions.stem: When a committee of the House of Representatives summons a minister to explain how funds were spent, it is performing its
questions.explanation: Oversight is the continuous scrutiny of how the executive implements laws and spends appropriated money. It is the natural companion to the power of appropriation: having voted the money, the legislature checks that it was properly used.

distractorRationale.b: The legislature's judicial function is confined to impeachment and contempt proceedings
distractorRationale.c: The representative function is voicing constituents' interests and grievances
distractorRationale.d: The constituent function refers to amending the Constitution

questions.stem: Members of both chambers of Nigeria's National Assembly are elected for a term of four years.
questions.explanation: True. Senators and members of the House of Representatives both serve four-year terms, running concurrently with the presidential term. Unlike some federations, Nigeria does not stagger senatorial elections.

distractorRationale.b: This would imply different terms for the two chambers, which the 1999 Constitution does not provide

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), section 64

questions.stem: A frequently cited disadvantage of a bicameral legislature is that it

options.text: makes law making slower and more expensive
concentrates all legislative power in one chamber

questions.explanation: Every bill must clear the full sequence of stages twice, and two sets of members, staff and buildings must be maintained. Delay and cost are the price paid for the extra check.

distractorRationale.a: The second chamber is designed precisely to represent smaller units
distractorRationale.c: Two chambers increase rather than prevent scrutiny
distractorRationale.d: Concentration in one chamber describes unicameralism
